name: Unicursal Labyrinth
desc: The classical unicursal labyrinth — one path, no junctions, no choice — cut as a worn channel into a full-frame pavement of jointed limestone, its lit and shadowed lips swapping sides as a lamp rakes slowly across the floor, while lit walkers thread the Cretan level sequence circuit by circuit toward a six-petal rosette and the whole floor precesses under them.

energy.doc: depth of the incision (how far the lit and shadowed lips separate), walker speed and lamp strength

scale.doc: labyrinth radius — 1 fills ~85% of the frame; at 2 you are standing inside two circuits

density.doc: number of walkers threading the path

speed.doc: how fast the walkers make the circuit

circuits.doc: circuit count — steps through the classical family 7 (Cretan) / 11 (Chartres) / 15 / 19

style.doc: stone: worn jointed limestone flags, the channel cut into them · turf: a sward maze with the path cut down to soil · blueprint: the setting-out drawing, no material at all · engraving: incised into toned laid paper · thread: pure abstraction — the material vanishes and only the single lit line remains

seed.doc: deterministic seed — same number, same floor
